chapter_plans.title: The Contract
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Grant Hart hires Calder Reed for a 21-day surveillance assignment on his separated wife Lena, and Calder immediately creates an evidence channel Grant does not control.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Grant hires Calder for a 21-day surveillance assignment ending on the settlement date; provides common-area camera access and the courtyard apartment. Calder activates his local archive and handwritten notebook; Grant receives only compressed reports. Primary turn: Calder accepts and creates an evidence channel Grant does not fully control.
must_happen: Grant explains his concern about Lena's instability and shows Calder the condominium layout, common-area camera feeds, and the courtyard-facing apartment.
Calder accepts the assignment, sets up recording equipment in the apartment, and activates his local archive system and handwritten field notebook.
Calder reviews Grant's written instructions and compresses the first daily report from test footage, establishing that Grant will not receive the unedited originals.
Calder observes the empty courtyard and notes the position of Lena's apartment windows, mentally marking the sightlines.
must_not: Do not reveal Lena's awareness of the surveillance or any suspicion about Calder's presence.
Do not include any romantic attraction, chemistry, or intimacy between Calder and Lena, even in thought or anticipation.
chapter_plans.opens_with: "You want to know if she's losing her mind, or if I'm making her lose it." Grant Hart slides a manila envelope across the conference table without waiting for my answer.
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: Calder watches the courtyard from his dark apartment; a light switches on in Lena's kitchen, and through the gap in her curtains he sees her silhouette moving with deliberate, unhurried precision.
chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: Calder notices that Grant's hands are steady, but the gold wedding band on his left hand is turned inward, the engraved surface facing his palm.
chapter_plans.emotional_beat: Calder feels a cold satisfaction at having the leverage of unedited originals, a professional reflex honed by years of distrusting clients.
chapter_plans.chapter_task: Write 1600-1900 words establishing Grant's manipulation, Calder's professional paranoia, and the setup of the surveillance operation. Focus on the contract negotiation and Calder's private recording decision.
chapter_plans.carries_to_next: Calder has established his baseline recording setup and local archive; Grant has delivered his narrative of Lena's instability; the surveillance is active.

chapter_plans.title: The Baseline
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Calder records Lena's ordinary routine, then witnesses a kitchen mug moved and Grant's immediate follow-up message, establishing the pattern of manufactured instability.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Calder records Lena's ordinary routine. After her walk she finds a kitchen mug moved; Grant messages moments later asking if she forgot something. Primary turn: Grant establishes Lena's alleged instability as Calder's baseline.
must_happen: Calder tracks Lena's morning routine from first light: she makes coffee, leaves for a walk at the same time, returns after exactly 28 minutes.
Through the common-area camera feed, Calder sees Lena return, pause in the kitchen, and stare at a mug that has been moved from its usual position on the counter.
Calder's phone buzzes with a compressed report from Grant: a screenshot of Lena's text asking if she forgot to put the mug away, and Grant's reply asking if she's been sleeping.
Calder reviews his unedited footage and notes that the mug was in its original position when Lena left; no one entered the apartment during her walk, meaning Grant has another access method.
must_not: Do not show Grant entering the apartment or explain how the mug was moved; keep the method ambiguous to Calder.
Do not include any romantic attraction or personal interest in Lena beyond professional observation.
chapter_plans.opens_with: At 6:47 AM, Lena Hart steps into her kitchen and pours coffee into the same ceramic mug she used yesterday, and I mark it as my first baseline data point.
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: Lena looks directly at the moved mug, then at her phone, then at the window—not at my window, but at the camera in the hallway corner above her door, and her expression shifts from confusion to something colder.
chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: Calder notes that the moved mug is the only object out of place in the entire apartment; everything else—the folded dish towel, the aligned coasters, the single orchid on the windowsill—is undisturbed.
chapter_plans.emotional_beat: Calder experiences a prickle of professional unease: the mug displacement is too precise, too isolated, to be simple forgetfulness, and Grant's timing is too convenient.
chapter_plans.chapter_task: Write 1600-1900 words depicting Lena's routine, the mug incident, and Calder's growing suspicion that Grant is manufacturing the instability. the unnamed contact's first-person POV and professional detachment.
chapter_plans.carries_to_next: Calder has witnessed Grant's manipulation but cannot prove it; Lena has shown the first sign of detecting the surveillance; Calder's baseline is contaminated by his own suspicion of the client.

chapter_plans.title: The Reflection
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Lena pauses at a status light reflected in Calder's window, detects the observer, and Calder becomes personally invested in her routine.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: The status light from Calder's courtyard camera reflects in his dark window. Lena pauses, looks first at the visible camera then at Calder's window, and continues. Canonical: Lena detects the observer here; prose does not explain it. Primary turn: Calder reads her pause as instinct and becomes personally invested.
must_happen: Calder continues recording Lena's routine; she follows the same schedule as the previous day, including the morning walk.

During Lena's return, the status light from Calder's courtyard camera reflects in his dark window; Lena stops, turns her head deliberately toward the visible hallway camera, then toward Calder's window, holds for three seconds, and continues into her apartment.
Calder rewinds the footage, watches the pause repeatedly, and cannot decide whether she saw the reflection or sensed something else.
Calder notes that after the pause, Lena changes one small behavior: she closes her kitchen curtains fully before making coffee, which she did not do on the previous day.
must_not: Do not reveal Lena's internal reasoning or confirm that she detected Calder; the prose must remain in Calder's uncertain POV.
Do not include any romantic attraction or personal desire; Calder's investment must be professional obsession and paranoia, not romantic interest.
chapter_plans.opens_with: The red status light on my camera glows for exactly three seconds during the power cycle, and I see it catch in my own window glass at the same moment Lena Hart turns her head.
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: Calder watches the closed kitchen curtains and realizes that Lena has just given him the first deliberate signal of her awareness—but whether it means she knows about him or simply dislikes being watched by the hallway camera, he cannot tell.
chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: The status light reflection appears not on the glass itself but on a thin layer of condensation, creating a ghost image that hovers in the air between Calder and the courtyard.
chapter_plans.emotional_beat: Calder feels a cold thrill of recognition: Lena is not the passive subject he assumed, and the surveillance has just become a contest he may not be winning.
chapter_plans.chapter_task: Write 1600-1900 words focusing on the moment of detection, Calder's analysis of the footage, and his shift from passive observer to engaged participant. Maintain uncertainty about Lena's knowledge.
chapter_plans.carries_to_next: Lena has detected the surveillance (canonical); Calder knows she changed her behavior but cannot confirm her awareness; the power dynamic has shifted, and Calder is now personally invested in watching her response.

chapter_plans.title: The Missing Mail
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Lena tells Mae Torres that a utility notice vanished from her mailbox; Grant later claims to have found it in the shared recycling, framing Lena as forgetful and Mae as an uncertain witness.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Lena reports a missing utility notice to Mae Torres in the lobby. Grant later claims he found the same notice in the shared recycling area, suggesting Lena discarded it and forgot. Mae is uncertain. Calder observes the exchange and notes Grant's pattern: converting an ordinary missing letter into witness-supported instability.
must_happen: Calder observes Lena and Mae Torres in the lobby; Lena shows Mae an empty mailbox and explains that a utility notice she placed there yesterday is gone.
Grant arrives, produces the same utility notice from his pocket, and claims he found it in the shared recycling bin; Lena's expression shifts from confusion to controlled anger.
Mae looks between them, uncertain; Calder notes that Grant has now created a witness who saw Lena 'forget' about a document she insisted was stolen.
Calder reviews his lobby footage and confirms that Grant entered the building through the board-access door during Lena's morning walk, consistent with the mug incident.
must_not: Do not reveal that Grant took the notice from Lena's mailbox; keep his method ambiguous to Calder.
Do not include any romantic attraction, chemistry, or intimacy between Calder and Lena.
chapter_plans.opens_with: "It was right here. I put it in the slot yesterday afternoon, and now it's gone." Lena Hart's voice carries through the lobby as she pulls the empty mailbox door open for Mae Torres to see.
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: Calder watches Grant walk away from the recycling bin and realizes that Grant is not just manufacturing instability—he is building a record with a living witness, and Calder is helping him do it.
chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: The utility notice is a generic county tax bill, but Calder notices the corner is slightly bent—identical to the crease on every document Grant handles, as if he folds them all the same way before planting them.
chapter_plans.emotional_beat: Calder feels a cold professional dread: he is documenting a pattern he now believes is fabricated, but his contract and evidence chain require him to continue recording.
chapter_plans.chapter_task: Write 1700-1900 words depicting the lobby confrontation, Calder's observation of Grant's method, and Calder's internal conflict about continuing the assignment. the unnamed contact's first-person POV and professional detachment.
chapter_plans.carries_to_next: Calder has witnessed Grant use Mae as an unwitting witness; Calder's suspicion of Grant's manipulation is now stronger than his professional neutrality; Lena has shown controlled anger rather than confusion.

chapter_plans.title: The Private Copy
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Calder watches Lena dance alone in her kitchen through the common-facing blinds, records it, but removes it from Grant's report; Lena places a folded red receipt beside the moved mug, building her physical timeline.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Calder observes Lena dance alone in her kitchen, visible through the common-facing blinds. He records it but deliberately excludes it from Grant's compressed report. Lena places a folded red receipt beside the previously moved mug, creating a physical marker. Primary turn: Calder begins keeping a private version of Lena he withholds from Grant.
must_happen: Calder watches Lena move through her kitchen in an unguarded moment: she sways to music only she can hear, a brief private dance visible through the common-facing blinds.
Calder records the dance but does not include it in the compressed report to Grant; he marks the footage for his local archive only.
Lena finishes her coffee, then deliberately places a folded red receipt on the counter beside the mug that Grant moved days earlier.
Calder notes the receipt's position and time-stamps it, recognizing it as a marker—either for her own memory or to test whether he is watching.
must_not: Do not describe any nudity, bedroom, or bathroom activity; the dance is fully clothed in the kitchen.
Do not include any romantic attraction, chemistry, or intimacy; Calder's decision to withhold footage is professional paranoia and personal investment in the evidence, not desire.
chapter_plans.opens_with: The music reaches me through the courtyard before I see her: a low bass line from a speaker I hadn't noticed in her kitchen, and then Lena Hart steps away from the counter and begins to move like no one is watching.
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: Calder closes the file on the dance footage and looks back at the live feed; Lena is standing at the counter, staring directly at her own window—not at his camera, but at the space where she danced—and she is smiling.
chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: The red receipt is from a hardware store Calder passed yesterday; the fold is precise, a triangle with the store logo centered, as if she prepared it before placing it.
chapter_plans.emotional_beat: Calder feels a sharp proprietary thrill at keeping the dance footage private, followed by unease that he is now actively choosing what Grant does not see.
chapter_plans.chapter_task: Write 1700-1900 words focusing on the dance moment, Calder's decision to exclude it from the report, and his observation of the red receipt marker. the unnamed contact's first-person POV and professional ambiguity about Lena's awareness.
chapter_plans.carries_to_next: Calder has established a private evidence channel separate from Grant's reports; Lena has placed a physical marker that Calder recognizes as a test; the power dynamic continues to shift.

chapter_plans.title: The Direct Look
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Lena repeats her routine with unnatural precision, then looks directly at Calder's dark window; Grant later asks whether Lena is 'performing for someone,' proving Grant reacts to reports but not that every detail reaches him.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Lena repeats her morning routine with exaggerated precision, each action timed to the second. She then stops, turns, and looks directly at Calder's dark window. Grant later messages Calder asking if Lena is 'performing for someone,' confirming Grant reacts to reports but not that every detail reaches him. Primary turn: Calder starts believing Lena may be communicating with him deliberately.
must_happen: Lena performs her morning routine with mechanical precision: coffee poured at exactly 6:47, walk begins at 6:52, returns at 7:20, each movement timed as if following a script.

After returning, Lena stands at the kitchen counter, turns her head slowly toward Calder's dark window, and holds his gaze—not at the hallway camera, but directly at his position—for a full five seconds.
Calder receives a message from Grant: 'Is she performing for someone? She seems different today.' Calder realizes Grant is reacting to his compressed report, but the direct look was not in it.
Calder rewinds the footage of the direct look and watches it multiple times, beginning to believe Lena is communicating with him—not with Grant, and not by accident.
must_not: Do not confirm Lena's internal reasoning; the prose must remain in Calder's uncertain POV.
Do not include any romantic attraction, chemistry, or intimacy; Calder's belief that Lena is communicating with him is professional and paranoid, not romantic.
chapter_plans.opens_with: At 6:47, Lena Hart pours her coffee. At 6:48, she sets the mug down. At 6:49, she takes her first sip. I have never seen anyone perform morning routine like a rehearsed stage block, but today she does.
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: Calder closes the footage file and looks at the live feed; Lena is now sitting at her kitchen table, writing in a paper planner, and she does not look up again—but the message has been delivered, and he received it.
chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: The direct look is held for exactly five seconds, which Calder later realizes is the same duration as the status light reflection in Chapter Three—she is mirroring the moment she first detected him.
chapter_plans.emotional_beat: Calder feels a cold certainty that he is no longer the only one watching the performance; Lena is watching him watch her, and she is in control of what he sees.
chapter_plans.chapter_task: Write 1700-1900 words depicting the precision routine, the direct look, Grant's reaction, and Calder's shift in understanding. the unnamed contact's first-person POV and uncertainty about Lena's intent.
chapter_plans.carries_to_next: Calder now believes Lena is deliberately communicating with him through her visible behavior; Grant has confirmed he reacts to reports but does not see everything; Calder's private archive and his growing personal investment are now in direct tension with his contract.

chapter_plans.title: The Deleted Minutes
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Calder witnesses Grant enter Lena's apartment during her walk and delete the dashboard interval; Calder preserves the original footage and omits it from the report, confirming Grant is manufacturing the instability.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Grant deletes a short dashboard interval; Calder's local original preserves it, showing Grant entering Lena's apartment with the master credential while she walks. Calder omits it from Grant's report, notes it in his notebook. Primary turn: Calder learns Grant is manufacturing the instability.
must_happen: Calder watches Lena leave for her morning walk at 6:52; the common-area feed shows Grant enter the building with a keycard, access Lena's door with a key, and exit five minutes later.
Calder's dashboard feed briefly goes dark for a two-minute interval covering Grant's entry; Calder checks his local archive and confirms the original footage is intact and unaltered.

Calder reviews the preserved footage: Grant enters Lena's apartment, moves a thermostat setting, and exits; Calder compares this with Grant's earlier message asking Lena if she forgot to adjust the heat.
Calder does not include the Grant-entry footage in his compressed report; he records the observation in his handwritten notebook and marks the original file as evidence.
must_not: Do not reveal Grant's internal reasoning or show him tampering with anything other than the thermostat and dashboard feed.
Do not include any romantic attraction, chemistry, or intimacy; Calder's decision to preserve the footage is professional paranoia and growing suspicion, not personal desire.
chapter_plans.opens_with: "The feed dropped for exactly one hundred and seventeen seconds." I say it aloud to no one, because speaking makes it real, and I need this to be real before I decide what it means.
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: Calder closes the original file and looks at the live feed; Lena returns from her walk, checks the thermostat, and stands motionless for ten seconds before reaching into her pocket and placing a folded red receipt beside the thermostat—her second deliberate marker.
chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: The thermostat's digital display shows 68°F when Lena left; after Grant's entry it reads 72°F; Lena adjusts it back to 68°F without checking the time, as if she already knew the change was coming.
chapter_plans.emotional_beat: Cold fury and professional betrayal: Calder realizes Grant has been manufacturing the instability he was hired to document, and Calder's own surveillance has been the tool.
chapter_plans.chapter_task: Write 1700-1900 words depicting the feed dropout, Calder's discovery of the preserved footage, and his decision to withhold the evidence from Grant. the unnamed contact's first-person POV and cold professional anger.
chapter_plans.carries_to_next: Calder now possesses irrefutable proof that Grant is entering Lena's apartment and altering details; Lena has placed a second red receipt as a marker; Calder's private archive has become a weapon against his client.

chapter_plans.title: The Honeytoken
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Calder follows Lena to a postal kiosk where she mails a certified envelope to herself; after delivery, Calder's lobby footage records Grant removing the clipped envelope with his duplicate key.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Calder follows Lena to a postal kiosk; she mails a certified envelope to herself, clips the lower-right corner, records the tracking number, folds a red receipt into her planner. After delivery, Calder's lobby footage records Grant removing the clipped envelope with the duplicate key; Grant opens it off-camera. Lena makes no accusation and does not know the removal was recorded. Primary turn: Lena creates an information-leak test whose full value neither she nor Calder yet grasps.
must_happen: Calder follows Lena as she leaves the condominium and walks to a postal kiosk; she fills out a certified mail form, mails a standard business envelope to her own address, clips the lower-right corner with small scissors from her bag, and records the tracking number in her paper planner.

Calder returns to his apartment and reviews the lobby camera feed; after the mail delivery, Grant enters the lobby with his keycard, opens Lena's mailbox with a key, removes the clipped envelope, and exits toward the basement.
Calder notes the envelope's clipped corner in his notebook and time-stamps the removal; he does not know the envelope's contents or Lena's purpose, but he recognizes the clip as a deliberate marker.

Lena collects the delivered envelope from her mailbox later that day; she checks the lower-right corner, confirms the clip is intact, and places the envelope unopened into her planner without visible reaction.
must_not: Do not reveal the envelope's contents or Lena's intent; the prose must remain in Calder's uncertain POV.
Do not include any romantic attraction, chemistry, or intimacy; Calder's observation is professional and paranoid, not personal.
chapter_plans.opens_with: Lena Hart steps out of the condominium lobby at 9:14 AM wearing a rain jacket she did not need—the sky is clear—and carrying a small padded envelope that was not in her hand five minutes ago.
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: Calder watches the lobby feed again and realizes that Grant removed the envelope with the same key he used to enter Lena's apartment, and that Calder's footage now connects Grant to two separate breaches—but he still does not know what is in the envelope or why Lena clipped the corner.
chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: The tracking number on Lena's certified receipt is 7013 1020 0001 2345; Calder memorizes it because the sequence is too orderly to be random, and he wonders whether Lena chose the number deliberately.
chapter_plans.emotional_beat: Professional curiosity sharpening into respect: Calder watches Lena build a trap he cannot yet see, and he begins to understand that she is not a victim waiting to be rescued.
chapter_plans.chapter_task: Write 1700-1900 words depicting the postal kiosk trip, the lobby footage of Grant's removal, and Calder's growing recognition that Lena is running a parallel operation. the unnamed contact's first-person POV and uncertainty about the envelope's purpose.
chapter_plans.carries_to_next: Calder has recorded Grant stealing Lena's mail; Lena has confirmed the clip is intact and knows the envelope was tampered with; Calder still does not know the contents or Lena's full plan, but he now has two pieces of physical evidence connecting Grant to deliberate interference.

chapter_plans.title: The Originals
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: In the laundry room, Lena holds a note toward the camera confirming Calder keeps originals; in the stairwell she confronts him, states Grant hired him, and offers a choice: keep serving Grant, preserve the truth without controlling her plan, or walk away.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: In the laundry room Lena holds a handwritten note toward the camera: "You keep the originals. Good." In the stairwell she states Grant hired him (part inference, part test); Calder confirms Grant gets only selected reports. She does not reveal the envelope's contents or purpose. She offers a choice: keep serving Grant, preserve the truth without taking control of her plan, or walk away. Primary turn: Calder and Lena acknowledge the surveillance and form a conditional alliance.
must_happen: Calder watches Lena enter the basement laundry room with her laundry basket; she positions herself directly in front of the common-area camera, holds a handwritten note reading "You keep the originals. Good." for five seconds, then folds it into her pocket.

Later that evening, Lena exits the stairwell door onto Calder's floor and confronts him in the hallway; she states that Grant hired him, that she inferred his surname from a lobby package label, and that she knows Calder keeps original footage Grant does not see.

Calder confirms that Grant receives only compressed reports and selected stills; Lena does not reveal the envelope's contents or her plan, but she states she needs a witness who preserves the truth without deciding what she should do with it.

Lena offers Calder three choices: continue serving Grant and report everything, preserve the evidence without controlling her decisions, or walk away entirely; Calder chooses to preserve the truth without taking control of her plan.
must_not: Do not reveal the envelope's contents or Lena's full plan; the confrontation establishes the alliance but withholds strategic details.
Do not include any romantic attraction, chemistry, or intimacy; the confrontation is tactical and professional, not personal or romantic.
chapter_plans.opens_with: "You keep the originals. Good." The words are written in black ink on a torn piece of notebook paper, and Lena Hart holds them flat against the camera lens in the laundry room as if she is showing a child how to read.
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: Lena turns to leave the stairwell, then pauses and says without turning around: "If you choose to stay, you will learn what is in the envelope. But not tonight. Tonight you sit with the fact that you chose to stop working for Grant before you knew what I was asking."
chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: The note is written on paper torn from the same planner Lena uses for her daily entries; the tear line matches the spiral-bound perforation, and Calder recognizes the paper stock from his earlier observations.
chapter_plans.emotional_beat: Relief and unease: Calder is no longer alone in his suspicion, but he has just committed to a path whose full cost he cannot calculate, and Lena has made it clear she will not explain until he proves his choice.
chapter_plans.chapter_task: Write 1800-1900 words depicting the laundry room note, the stairwell confrontation, and Calder's decision to align with Lena. the unnamed contact's first-person POV and the weight of choosing against his client.
chapter_plans.carries_to_next: Calder has acknowledged the surveillance to Lena and chosen to preserve the evidence; Lena has confirmed his role and set the terms of their conditional alliance; the envelope's contents remain unknown to Calder, and the next phase of the plan begins.

chapter_plans.title: The Terms
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Lena explains Grant is manufacturing evidence to force her out before the settlement and sets explicit rules for Calder's access; Calder agrees, keeps sending Grant edited reports of staged behavior.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Lena explains Grant is manufacturing evidence to force her out before the settlement. Rules: no recording device in her apartment; the courtyard camera never records nudity or sex; Calder disables and covers it before entering; no physical contact without a direct yes; no private image to Grant; no decisions on her behalf; consent withdrawable without negotiation; preserve but never fabricate evidence; Lena controls when the alliance ends. Calder agrees, keeps sending Grant edited reports of staged behavior. Primary turn: relationship shifts from unilateral surveillance to negotiated access.
must_happen: Lena explains that Grant has been manufacturing evidence — moving objects, altering the thermostat, removing mail — to build a record that she cannot safely maintain the jointly owned apartment before the settlement.

Lena states the rules for any ongoing contact: no recording device inside her apartment, the courtyard camera must never record nudity or sex, Calder must disable and cover the lens before entering, no physical contact without a direct verbal yes, no private image to Grant, no decisions on her behalf, consent withdrawable without negotiation, preserve but never fabricate evidence, and she controls when the alliance ends.
Calder agrees to the terms; he composes a compressed report for Grant showing staged behavior (a harmless visible packing action) and omits any reference to the confrontation or the new rules.
Calder disables the courtyard camera's audio feed and covers the lens with a lens cap before entering Lena's apartment for the first time under the new terms; Lena verifies no device is active.

chapter_plans.opens_with: "You think he's just forgetful, don't you?" Lena Hart says, standing in her own kitchen with her arms crossed, the red receipt still visible on the counter beside the thermostat. "He's not forgetful, Calder. He's manufacturing."
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: Calder steps back into the hallway, the door clicking shut behind him, and realizes that for the first time in seven weeks he entered Lena's apartment not to watch her but because she chose to let him — and that she verified his equipment was off before he crossed the threshold.
chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: Lena keeps a small brass key — the duplicate mailbox key — on a red lanyard hung from the edge of her planner, visible but never mentioned aloud.
chapter_plans.emotional_beat: Calder experiences a cold, tactical clarity: he has chosen against his client and must now manage Grant's expectations while preserving the evidence chain; there is no relief, only the weight of the decision.
chapter_plans.chapter_task: Write 1700-1900 words depicting the rule-setting conversation, Calder's agreement, and his first entry into Lena's apartment under the new terms. the unnamed contact's first-person POV and professional detachment.
chapter_plans.carries_to_next: Calder has accepted Lena's terms and entered her apartment under negotiated access; he continues sending Grant edited reports of staged behavior; the envelope's contents remain unknown.

chapter_plans.opens_with: "The hallway floor is clear. Leave your bag there." Lena Hart gestures to the spot beside her door, and Calder sets down the equipment case he has carried through every observation shift for seven weeks.
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: Calder lies in the dark of Lena's apartment, listening to her breathe, and understands that she has shown him only what she chose to show — and that the part of her plan he cannot see is the part that matters most.
chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: Lena's planner has a small brass key — the duplicate mailbox key — clipped to the spiral binding on a red lanyard; Calder notices it but does not ask.

chapter_plans.title: The Returned Phrase
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Grant tells Calder to watch for packing and asks if Lena seems ready for a 'Friday key return'; Lena shows Calder the false checklist with the same phrase, confirming Grant intercepted the envelope; Calder's footage adds physical corroboration.

Calder tells her his footage also shows Grant taking the envelope; the test gains a second layer. Grant separately orders Calder to photograph unsafe interior conditions; Calder refuses, claiming exterior observation is more credible; Lena stages one harmless visible packing action to preserve Grant's confidence. Primary turn: the envelope proves theft, then gains physical corroboration.
must_happen: Grant messages Calder: 'Watch for packing. Does she seem ready for a Friday key return?' Calder has never heard the phrase and notes it in his notebook.

Calder tells Lena that his unedited lobby footage also shows Grant removing the clipped envelope from her mailbox with the duplicate key, providing physical corroboration beyond the phrase itself.
